hints: Particle $A$ ($3\text{ kg}$) has initial speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and particle $B$ ($6\text{ kg}$) is at rest.
After impact, $A$ moves with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. It could either continue forward ($v_A = +2$) or rebound ($v_A = -2$).
Apply conservation of momentum for both cases to find $v_B$: $3(8) = 3(v_A) + 6(v_B)$.
Calculate the kinetic energy loss $KE_{\text{initial}} - KE_{\text{final}}$ for each case and state the greater loss.
walkthrough: Let us consider both physical possibilities for the velocity of particle $A$ after the collision:

Given data:
$$m_A = 3\text{ kg},\quad u_A = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$m_B = 6\text{ kg},\quad u_B = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The speed of $A$ after collision is $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so its velocity $v_A$ could be either $+2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ or $-2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Initial kinetic energy of the system:
$$KE_i = \frac{1}{2}m_A u_A^2 + \frac{1}{2}m_B u_B^2 = \frac{1}{2}(3)(8^2) + 0 = 1.5 \times 64 = 96\text{ J}$$
Case 1: Particle $A$ continues in its original direction ($v_A = +2\text{ m s}^{-1}$).

By conservation of momentum:
$$m_A u_A = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$$
$$3(8) = 3(2) + 6v_B$$
$$24 = 6 + 6v_B$$
$$6v_B = 18 \implies v_B = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Kinetic energy loss in Case 1:
$$\Delta KE_1 = 96 - 33 = 63\text{ J}$$

By conservation of momentum:
$$3(8) = 3(-2) + 6v_B$$
$$24 = -6 + 6v_B$$
$$6v_B = 30 \implies v_B = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Kinetic energy loss in Case 2:
$$\Delta KE_2 = 96 - 81 = 15\text{ J}$$
Comparing both cases, the greater possible loss of kinetic energy is $63\text{ J}$.
